cls: Dopamine precursor (aromatic amino acid; antiparkinson agent)
quick: With carbidopa, e.g. carbidopa 25 mg/levodopa 100 mg orally 3 times daily, titrated
Take consistently; high-protein meals can reduce levodopa absorption
Limited data; use only if benefit outweighs risk
May suppress lactation; caution - limited infant data
Use with caution; limited data, generally no fixed adjustment
Use with caution in significant hepatic impairment
Avoid/limit - may worsen drowsiness and orthostatic hypotension
Motor response, BP (orthostatic), mood, impulse-control behaviors
summary: Levodopa is the metabolic precursor of dopamine and is the most effective drug for the motor symptoms of Parkinson disease. It is almost always given WITH carbidopa (a peripheral DOPA-decarboxylase inhibitor that does not cross the blood-brain barrier); carbidopa prevents peripheral conversion of levodopa to dopamine, increasing the fraction reaching the brain and reducing peripheral side effects such as nausea, so much lower levodopa doses are needed and levodopa alone is now rarely used. Long-term therapy is complicated by motor fluctuations (wearing-off, on-off), dyskinesias, and impulse control disorders. Levodopa therapy must NOT be stopped abruptly because of the risk of a neuroleptic malignant syndrome-like reaction.
indications: Treatment of the symptoms of idiopathic Parkinson disease (paralysis agitans)
Post-encephalitic parkinsonism and symptomatic parkinsonism following carbon monoxide or manganese intoxication
Parkinsonism that may accompany other conditions, in combination with carbidopa

dosage.d: Carbidopa 25 mg/levodopa 100 mg 2-3 times daily (or carbidopa 12.5 mg/levodopa 50 mg)
dosage.n: Levodopa is almost always combined with carbidopa; titrate slowly to response

dosage.d: Increase by 1 tablet of carbidopa 25 mg/levodopa 100 mg every 1-2 days as needed (slower titration over weeks improves tolerability)
dosage.n: Goal is the lowest dose giving a satisfactory clinical response

dosage.d: Typically carbidopa/levodopa providing about 75-200 mg carbidopa and 750-1500 mg levodopa per day in divided doses
dosage.n: At least 70-100 mg/day of carbidopa is needed to fully inhibit peripheral decarboxylase

dosage.d: Usual maximum about carbidopa 200 mg/day and levodopa 2000 mg (2 g)/day
dosage.n: Adjust for advanced disease and motor fluctuations; do not stop abruptly

dosage.d: Much higher doses (up to several grams/day) are required; rarely used
dosage.n: Carbidopa reduces the required levodopa dose by about 75% and limits peripheral effects

admin: Levodopa is almost always given WITH carbidopa; carbidopa blocks peripheral conversion of levodopa to dopamine
Administer at consistent times; spacing doses away from high-protein meals can improve absorption
Titrate the dose slowly to balance motor benefit against dyskinesia and adverse effects
Do NOT discontinue abruptly - taper gradually to avoid a neuroleptic malignant syndrome-like reaction
When switching from levodopa alone, stop levodopa at least 12 hours before starting a carbidopa-levodopa product
Discontinue nonselective MAO inhibitors at least 2 weeks before starting levodopa
moa: Levodopa crosses the blood-brain barrier and is decarboxylated by aromatic L-amino acid (DOPA) decarboxylase to dopamine within the central nervous system, replenishing depleted striatal dopamine in Parkinson disease. Dopamine itself does not cross the blood-brain barrier. When co-administered, carbidopa inhibits peripheral DOPA decarboxylase but does not cross the blood-brain barrier, so more levodopa is available to enter the brain and peripheral dopaminergic side effects (nausea, vomiting, cardiovascular effects) are reduced.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to levodopa or carbidopa
Concurrent use of nonselective MAO inhibitors (must be stopped at least 2 weeks beforehand)
relative: Suspicious undiagnosed skin lesions or history of melanoma (levodopa may activate melanoma)
History of psychosis or major psychiatric disorder
Severe cardiovascular disease, arrhythmias, or recent myocardial infarction
Wide-angle glaucoma (use with caution and monitor intraocular pressure)
monitor: Cardiovascular status and orthostatic blood pressure
Mental status and impulse control / compulsive behaviors
Signs of melanoma; periodic skin examination

preg: There are limited human data. Levodopa and dopamine can affect uterine and fetal physiology; use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: Levodopa is excreted in human milk and may suppress lactation by inhibiting prolactin. Use caution while breastfeeding; data on effects in the breastfed infant are limited.
renal: Specific dose adjustments are not well defined; use with caution in renal impairment and monitor for adverse effects, as levodopa metabolites are renally excreted.
hepatic: Use with caution in patients with significant hepatic impairment; no specific dose adjustment is firmly established, but monitor closely.

major: Nonselective MAO inhibitors - hypertensive crisis; contraindicated, stop at least 2 weeks before levodopa
Dopamine antagonists / antipsychotics (e.g., haloperidol, metoclopramide) - reduce levodopa efficacy and may worsen parkinsonism
moderate: Iron salts - chelate levodopa/carbidopa and reduce absorption
Pyridoxine (vitamin B6) - increases peripheral decarboxylation of levodopa (largely mitigated by carbidopa)
Selective MAO-B inhibitors (selegiline, rasagiline) - risk of hypotension; use with care
Isoniazid and phenytoin - may reduce levodopa effect
minor: Metoclopramide - increases gastric emptying but is a dopamine antagonist
interactions.food: High-protein meals provide large neutral amino acids that compete with levodopa for absorption and transport into the brain, reducing its effect; keep protein intake and dose timing consistent.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid or limit alcohol, which may worsen drowsiness, dizziness, and orthostatic hypotension.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false-positive urine ketone tests and false readings on urine glucose tests; can transiently affect catecholamine and uric acid measurements.

serious: Dyskinesias and disabling motor fluctuations (wearing-off, on-off phenomenon)
Impulse control disorders (pathological gambling, hypersexuality, compulsive shopping/eating)
Neuroleptic malignant syndrome-like reaction on abrupt withdrawal
rare: Gastrointestinal bleeding (in patients with prior peptic ulcer)
emergency: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome-like syndrome (hyperthermia, rigidity, altered consciousness) after abrupt dose reduction or withdrawal
Severe hypertensive crisis if taken with nonselective MAOIs
Acute psychosis with danger to self or others

monitoring: Motor response and parkinsonian symptoms; emergence of dyskinesias and motor fluctuations
Mental status, mood, and signs of impulse control or compulsive behaviors
Daytime sleepiness and episodes of sudden sleep onset
Intraocular pressure in patients with glaucoma
Skin examination for melanoma; periodic CBC, hepatic, renal, and cardiovascular evaluation with long-term use
counsel: This medicine is usually taken with carbidopa; do not stop taking it suddenly - stopping abruptly can cause a dangerous reaction with fever and muscle rigidity
Rise slowly from sitting or lying to reduce dizziness; report fainting
Tell your doctor about urges to gamble, shop, eat, or other compulsive behaviors - these can be caused by the medicine
You may fall asleep suddenly; use caution when driving or operating machinery
Avoid high-protein meals at the same time as your dose, and keep your dosing schedule consistent
Report new or worsening involuntary movements, hallucinations, confusion, or mood changes; harmless darkening of urine/sweat can occur
pk: Symptomatic benefit within 30-60 minutes of an oral immediate-release dose
Plasma peak about 0.5-2 hours after an immediate-release dose
Levodopa about 50 minutes alone; about 1.5 hours when given with carbidopa
Short - clinical effect a few hours; controlled-release/adjuncts prolong it
Store at 20-25 C (excursions 15-30 C); protect from moisture and light
pearls: Levodopa is almost always combined with carbidopa - carbidopa inhibits peripheral DOPA decarboxylase (does not enter the brain), cutting the required levodopa dose by ~75% and reducing nausea
At least 70-100 mg/day of carbidopa is needed to fully saturate peripheral decarboxylase
Long-term use leads to motor fluctuations (wearing-off, on-off) and levodopa-induced dyskinesias related to peak plasma levels
Screen for impulse control disorders (gambling, hypersexuality, compulsive shopping/eating)
NEVER stop abruptly - withdrawal can precipitate a neuroleptic malignant syndrome-like reaction
High-protein meals and pyridoxine reduce levodopa effect; nonselective MAOIs are contraindicated
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule; do not take two doses at once. Do not stop the medicine on your own.
overdose: Acute overdose may cause severe nausea and vomiting, cardiac arrhythmias, marked hypertension or hypotension, agitation, confusion, and dyskinesias. There is no specific antidote; manage supportively with ECG and cardiovascular monitoring, airway protection, and treatment of arrhythmias and hypotension. Pyridoxine does not reverse carbidopa-levodopa effects.
